# Program status: the research tech tree {#sec-program-status}

**This chapter is the one place in the book that is a live status ledger
rather than settled knowledge.** The program is run as a tech tree: every
experiment is a node with a preregistered question, the nodes it depends
on, an acceptance criterion written before the run, and a dated verdict in
the lab notebook (@sec-notebook). A polished chapter cites a result only
once its node is DONE here. Because this is a ledger, it is also the one
chapter where dates and node codes appear; everywhere else an experiment is
named by what it measures.

**How to read status.** Each node carries one of six words, written in its
label and repeated in the ledger: PLANNED (a prerequisite is unmet), READY
(can start now), RUNNING (has an active job or owner), BLOCKED (needs an
external resolution), DONE (its acceptance criterion was met or its
falsifier fired), STOPPED (deliberately
abandoned, refuted, or superseded). Shape and border repeat the word:
DONE nodes are plain boxes with a green border, RUNNING nodes are rounded
boxes with a blue fill, PLANNED and READY nodes are hexagons with a dashed
grey border, STOPPED nodes are stadium shapes with a grey fill. An arrow
from A to B means B could not start until A produced what it needed. The
tree is drawn as five thematic sub-trees; a node appears in one sub-tree
and its full dependency list is in the ledger's fourth column. Ratios
follow the book's convention, baseline error divided by ISLA error.

## The tech tree {#sec-tech-tree}

### Foundations and the reframing

The early nodes set the question (generalization measured as curves, not
points), audited ISLA's own contracts, and ended in an independent critic
review that reframed the program around the fair-comparison protocol.

%%|   program, appears only here (G3, G3K, K0) and in the interior sub-tree
%%|   (V0).

## The ledger {#sec-ledger}

One row per node, in the order of the sub-trees. The "Depends on" column is
the full dependency list, including edges the sub-trees do not draw. Every
evidence link goes to the dated notebook entry holding the preregistration
and the verdict; rows whose comparison was against baselines fed the
physical freestream velocity say "superseded as a comparison" and keep
their numbers as measurements of that protocol only.

| ID | Status | Question and why it matters | Depends on / starts if | Acceptance criterion | Evidence or result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NSTAR | DONE | Reframe the goal: measure generalization as curves (error against training-set size and beyond the training hull), not points. | — | Preregistered framing adopted with a declared ladder design. | @sec-nb-generalization-northstar |
| G1G2 | DONE | Do ISLA's contracts improve accuracy per sample, and does zero-shot transfer improve with in-family data? | NSTAR | 22-lane nested ladder, two seeds per rung, preregistered predictions scored. | @sec-nb-g1g2-verdict |
| LOC | DONE (refuted) | Is GeoTransolver's data-compounding transfer carried by local features? | G1G2 | Monotone zero-shot decrease with ISLA's local channel; a flat curve refutes. Flat: a constant 3 to 5% in-family offset only. | @sec-nb-locality-verdict |
| M1 | DONE (verdict void) | Is exact scale equivariance an over-symmetrization? | G1G2 | Over 5% in-family gain from scale conditioning at 218 cars. Read as refuted, then voided by CRIT: the constant gauge already fed absolute size. | @sec-nb-m1-verdict-wave-close; @sec-nb-critic-review |
| M2 | DONE (closed) | Does anchor-conditioned decoding recover the accuracy the passive decode lost? | G1G2 | Pilot validation loss at most 0.01500; measured 0.01517. Re-opened resource-matched as V6. | @sec-nb-v5a4-gate; @sec-nb-campaign-review |
| M3 | DONE (partial) | Does the invariant-only feature set have a provable expressivity ceiling? | G1G2 | Constructed pairs separate at roundoff against controls. Ceiling real; not established as a cause on cars; a reflection defect in the vector head opened PAR. | @sec-nb-m3-verdict; @sec-nb-audit-2026-09-08 |
| M4 | DONE (retracted, then refuted) | Does ISLA miss a measure-weighted normalization that explains the density floor? | G1G2 | Closed by derivation, retracted by CRIT (unweighted centroid), refuted by S1 (weighted gauge cuts the penalty from 13 to 14.5x to 1.20x). | @sec-nb-lit-wave-prereg; @sec-nb-critic-review; @sec-nb-s1-verdict |
| G3 | DONE (one verdict overturned) | Which boundary-condition generalization axes can architecture improve, on an exact 2D Laplace suite? | NSTAR | Per-axis degradation fingerprints. Amplitude extrapolation exact under linearity stands; the frequency verdict was overturned by G3K. | @sec-nb-g3-verdict; @sec-nb-g3-kernel-rerun |
| HL | DONE | Does the DrivAerML frontier extend to Reynolds-varying physics on the HiLiftAeroML full split? | G1G2, LOC, M1 | Preregistered readouts with the learning-rate parity amendment. | V6 | DONE | Does anchor-conditioned decode win at matched peak memory? | M2 | Closure bar 1.3x; measured 3.1x worse. | @sec-nb-instrument-wave-verdict |

: The tech-tree ledger, one row per node. Statuses are as of 2026-09-18. Evidence links go to the dated lab-notebook entry holding the preregistration and verdict; where a node's verdict was later voided, retracted or overturned, the status says so and the row links both entries. {#tbl-tech-tree}

## Provenance {#sec-provenance}

Every quantitative claim in the polished chapters is computed live from a
checked-in artifact under `examples/cfd/mesh_transformer/results/` (JSON
reductions of evaluation runs, each named with the date of the run that
produced it), or is a literal quoted from one of those files with the file
named in the caption. The lab notebook (@sec-notebook) holds, for every
artifact, the preregistration that preceded the run, the launch record,
and the verdict entry; the ledger above links each node to those entries.
Training runs, checkpoints and per-point predictions live on the cluster in
the task directory named in the notebook and are not needed to regenerate
any figure in this book.

Two protocol facts a reader should carry into every chapter: all HiLift and
DrivAerML training runs used the same frozen recipe (10,000 sampled surface
points per case, 500 epochs, bfloat16, no augmentation, two or more seeds),
and every sealed test split was evaluated exactly once under a configuration
committed before the first test case was read. Where a claim rests on a
two-seed comparison the text says so; where a paired per-case statistic
exists it is reported instead of, not in addition to, an adjective.
